title: Garden Egg Stew with Dried Shrimp
author: Naa Adjei
desc: Skinned and de-seeded rather than mashed, with a cup each of palm oil and dried shrimp, and a final thirty to forty minutes on low.
longDesc: The other way to make garden egg stew: boil the eggs twelve to fifteen minutes, then remove the skin and the seeds and dice the flesh, so you get distinct pieces rather than a paste. A cup of palm oil is heated three to five minutes, the onion fried three, then red pepper powder and nutmeg for three more before a cup of dried shrimp goes in. Blended tomato simmers fifteen minutes, a cup of water twenty, then the fish and garden eggs return for a long final thirty to forty minutes on low heat.
ingredients: 8 large tomatoes, or 1 tin tomato purée
steps: Boil the garden eggs 12 to 15 minutes.
Remove the skin and seeds and dice the flesh.
Heat the palm oil 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the red pepper powder and nutmeg and cook 3 minutes.
Add the blended tomato mix and simmer 15 minutes.
Add 1 cup of water and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the fish and the diced garden eggs.
Let the stew simmer another 30 to 40 minutes on low heat.
chefTips: Skin AND de-seed, then dice. That is what makes this stew chunky where the other documented version is a paste — the two are genuinely different dishes.
The seeds are where most of garden egg's bitterness sits, so removing them gives a much milder stew. Keep them in if the bitterness is what you want.
A cup of dried shrimp is a large amount and it is the backbone of the dish — it supplies all the savoury depth that dawadawa does in the other version.
Heat the palm oil three to five minutes before the onion. That drives off the raw edge without bleaching it.
Thirty to forty minutes on low at the end, after everything else. It is a long finish and it is where the stew comes together.
Nutmeg here but no aniseed, against both in the other version. A teaspoon is a lot of nutmeg and it will be prominent.
No doneness cue is printed anywhere on this page — only times. Judge the end by the oil sitting clear on the surface.
commonMistakes: Mashing rather than dicing, which makes it the other recipe.
Leaving the seeds in if you want it mild.
Adding the onion to cold palm oil.
Cutting the final low simmer short.
Reducing the dried shrimp, which leaves the stew flat.
sources: Adapted from 'Traditional Ghanaian recipes • Garden egg stew', Time Out Accra, 7 June 2013. BYLINE FLAG: NO AUTHOR is credited; the publication is cited rather than an individual. NO YIELD and NO DONENESS CUE appear on the page. Ingredients are SINGLE-PASS and therefore unverified against a second fetch.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 9 garden eggs; 8 large tomatoes or 1 can of tomato puree; 2 large white onions; 1 tablespoon red pepper powder; 1 habanero pepper; 1 teaspoon nutmeg; 1 small ginger root (grated); 1/2 lb steamed or dried fish; 1 cup dried shrimp; 1 cup palm oil; Salt (to taste). Plus the cup of water from the method.

Method as printed: boil the garden eggs 12-15 minutes, then remove skin and seeds and dice; heat palm oil 3-5 minutes; fry the diced onion 3 minutes, add pepper powder and nutmeg for 3 minutes, then the dried shrimp; add the blended tomato mix and simmer 15 minutes; add 1 cup water and simmer 20 minutes; add fish and garden eggs. FINAL STEP, verbatim: 'Let the stew simmer for another 30-40 minutes on low heat.'
NO SENSORY ENDPOINT EXISTS on this page. The oil-on-the-surface guidance in the tips is general West African stew practice and is NOT asserted as sourced.

'8 large tomatoes or 1 can of tomato puree' is a very loose equivalence — eight large fresh tomatoes is far more than a standard tin of purée. The source offers them as alternatives and neither is adjusted here.
'1 small ginger root' is not a quantity and has not been converted.

THE PEEL-AND-DE-SEED METHOD is what distinguishes this version and is the reason it is published separately from GHA026. Akwasi Brenya-Mensa mashes the whole cooked garden egg to a paste; this recipe discards skin and seeds and dices the flesh. Since the seeds carry most of the bitterness, the two stews taste substantially different. Neither is corrected toward the other.
For the full three-way disagreement across the documented garden egg stews — method, palm oil quantity and cooking times — see the sources at GHA026.
reheating: Gentle heat until the palm oil re-melts.
healthBenefits: Dried shrimp is very high in protein, calcium and iodine.
Garden egg provides fibre, folate and polyphenols.
Red palm oil supplies provitamin-A carotenoids.
High in lycopene from the long-cooked tomato.
culturalNote: Whether you mash garden eggs or dice them is the kind of household decision that never gets argued about in print but splits kitchens completely. The diced version keeps the vegetable visible on the plate; the mashed one turns it into the sauce itself. Both are called garden egg stew and nobody in Ghana would be confused by either.
